newsitem.title: USA: BASF sees Gulf Coast cracker start by 2000.
newsitem.headline: BASF sees Gulf Coast cracker start by 2000.

text.p: BASF AG's BASF Corp said Wednesday preliminary plans for a steam cracker to be built on the Gulf Coast call for a possible startup within four years.

"The results of our project analysis have been extremely encouraging and we will proceed with high priority to have the cracker ready for startup in the second half of the year 2000," said Carl Jennings, president of BASF's chemicals division.

The company said it will decide by mid-1997 where on the Gulf Coast the new unit will be located. In addition to the three BASF sites at Geismar, La.; Freeport, La.; and Altamira, Mexico, other cooperative arrangements are also under consideration, it said.
The cracker is planned to have flexible feedstock capability and an annual capacity of 1.5 billion pounds of ethylene and 900 million pounds of propylene.
BASF said it expects the new cracker will provide sufficient ethylene capacity to supply its existing plants as well as potential external customers in the Gulf Coast area.
It said its expansion will include investments in infrastructure and logistics to appropriately position the new facility for future growth in the NAFTA Region.
BASF Corp is the U.S. unit of Germany's BASF AG group. The unit, with sales of $6.3 billion in 1996, is among the top 10 producers of chemicals in the United States.
